newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Pope departs Sarajevo after historic visit.
newsitem.headline: Pope departs Sarajevo after historic visit.

text.p: Pope John Paul II left Sarajevo on Sunday after calling on Bosnians to forsake the nationalist hatred that fuelled a devastating war.

The Pope's Alitalia plane took off for Rome at about 6:45 p.m. (1600 GMT) from heavily-guarded Sarajevo airport. The Pontiff went ahead with his 25-hour visit despite an apparent assassination threat uncovered shortly before his arrival.
Before the Pope travelled to Sarajevo on Saturday, Bosnian police removed explosives attached to a remote control system along his motorcade route.
Authorities had yet to report any arrests or other details in the case.
In a speech at the airport, the Pope said lasting peace could only be built on tolerance among the country's Moslems, Catholic Croats and Orthodox Christian Serbs.
"To succeed ...you must call upon your best energies and cooperate with all the people of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the knowledge that all are brothers and sisters, for all are children of the one God."
